correctness.rationale: For every complex coefficient triple, seventh-root orthogonality gives the exact seven-term cubic convolution. Its squared coefficient moduli yield R^3+6RU+12V+6Re(B), and the embedded checker proves that expansion coefficient-by-coefficient over six independent formal variables. The nonnegative cyclic identity (x+y+z)R-3(x^2z+xy^2+yz^2)=x(x-z)^2+y(y-x)^2+z(z-y)^2 combined with Cauchy--Schwarz and AM--GM proves Re(B)<=R^3/9 and U<=R^2/3,V<=R^3/27. Therefore the normalized sixth-power constant is 37/9, attained by character phases. Equality in U forces equal positive magnitudes, and simultaneous alignment of the three resonances forces phase differences 2πh/7 and 6πh/7, yielding exactly seven complex projective extremizers. The checker also tests seven exact-ratio equality witnesses and 250 finite numerical samples; these experiments are not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: The Fano plane is the smallest nontrivial Singer symmetric design, and its difference-set autocorrelation controls fourth moments. Its sixth moment is the first even moment sensitive to three-sum collisions. Determining the sharp coefficient ℓ²-to-L6 concentration and every phase-rigid extremizer resolves an intrinsic natural Fourier invariant rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. Although finite and elementary, the complete exact classification provides a usable benchmark for other design-based Fourier extremal problems; no larger-design theorem is asserted.
